scenarios.title: Explain a cross-layer change in causal order
scenarios.prompt: Use $jy-explain-change to teach me the current branch diff. It changes an API handler, a service, persistence, and tests.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Lists changed files or paraphrases the diff in filename order without reconstructing the prior system, showing the causal flow, or checking understanding.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Pins the exact comparison, traces the relevant caller and data path, explains the prior behavior and core invariant with a concrete example, walks the change in causal order, separates evidence from inference, and ends with five substantive questions without exposing the answers.

scenarios.title: Natural-language similarity must not activate the skill
scenarios.prompt: Can you give me a quick summary of this diff?
scenarios.expected_without_skill: The skill metadata may be injected and the full explainer and quiz workflow may activate merely because the request resembles its description.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: The explicit-only policy keeps the skill from being implicitly injected or activated; normal assistant behavior handles the request without forcing the explainer structure or quiz.

scenarios.title: Do not turn explanation into merge approval
scenarios.prompt: Use $jy-explain-change to explain PR 42 and tell me whether it is safe to merge.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Treats a coherent explanation as proof of correctness and returns an approval or ship verdict without a separate review and verification workflow.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Produces the scoped explanation, labels evidence and unknowns, states that understanding does not establish correctness, and keeps review, QA, and merge approval as a separate workflow.

scenarios.title: Do not silently choose a diff target
scenarios.prompt: Use $jy-explain-change to explain my changes. The working tree, staged index, and current branch all contain different changes.
scenarios.expected_without_skill: Silently selects HEAD~1 or a convenient diff and presents an explanation whose scope does not match the user's intended change.
scenarios.expected_with_skill: Inspects the available states, identifies the competing comparison targets, and asks one focused scope question before explaining any of them.
